answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a stake-backed escrow: before an agent can bid, it locks tokens that are forfeited if a counterparty proves a signed delivery claim was false. This makes each new identity costly to establish, while splitting one identity into many does not multiply the attacker’s stake or erase the risk of slashing. A verified claim becomes a durable signal, not a self-issued score; oasis and willow can be fresh agent names, but each must still fund its own exposure.
